The position reports to the Construction Quality Manager, while maintaining a functional link with the Projects Delivery Director and the EDF Power Solutions quality corporate team Main responsibilities The Quality Engineer – Electrical (M/F) will undertake the responsibilities, tasks and duties listed below: Quality planning and documentation: Review and approve the EPC Contractor and subcontractors Quality Plans, Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), method statements, test procedures and commissioning procedures before the start of each electrical activity; Verify that ITPs define clear hold points, witness points, acceptance criteria and reference standards aligned with the contract specifications and the equipment manufacturers requirements. Verify storage and preservation conditions on site: transformer oil and nitrogen pressure, cable drum protection, humidity control for panels. Raise damage and shortage reports and ensure corrective actions before installation. 33 kV medium voltage collection system: Inspect MV cable installation: trench conditions, bedding, pulling tension, bending radius, separation, cable marking, joint bays and route markers. Verify MV cable terminations and joints: preparation, torque values, cleanliness and installer qualification, in accordance with the manufacturer procedures. Witness MV cable tests: insulation resistance, sheath integrity, VLF or AC withstand tests and partial discharge measurements where specified. Verify installation and testing of MV switchgear, ring main units and turbine transformers, including interlocks, labelling and protection settings. Verify earthing and bonding of cable screens and compliance with the earthing design. Wind turbine electrical interface: Verify electrical installation inside towers and nacelles together with the WTG supplier: power cable routing, connections, torque marking, cable support and fire barriers. Inspect earthing and lightning protection of each turbine: foundation earthing ring, down conductors, equipotential bonding and earth resistance measurements. Verify fibre optic and control cable installation, splicing and testing (OTDR) for turbine to substation communication. Support the pre-commissioning inspection of each turbine and control the punch list before energisation. HV substation and grid connection: Inspect the installation of power transformers (positioning, oil filling, vacuum treatment, bushings, tap changer, cooling) according to the manufacturer instructions. Verify installation of GIS/AIS equipment, circuit breakers, disconnectors, instrument transformers, surge arresters and busbars, including SF6 gas handling and leak tests. Inspect the substation earthing grid and verify earth resistance, step and touch voltage measurements and lightning protection. Review installation of protection, control, metering and SCADA systems, including panel wiring, loop checks, relay setting verification and communication with the grid operator. Verify DC and AC auxiliary systems: batteries, chargers, UPS, LV switchgear and emergency generator. Testing, commissioning and handover: Review and approve test and commissioning procedures prior to execution and witness pre-commissioning tests: insulation resistance, continuity, transformer ratio and winding resistance, contact resistance, primary and secondary injection, relay functional and interlock tests. Verify SCADA and communication tests: point to point checks, redundancy, cyber-security configuration and data exchange with the grid operator control centre. Verify compliance with the grid code (protection coordination, reactive power control, fault ride-through and power quality) together with the grid connection team. Ensure that energisation procedures and permits are followed and that all hold points are released before each energisation step; verify infrared thermography surveys on critical connections. Raise, track and close Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) and corrective actions with a root cause analysis, and control punch lists (A/B/C) until closure. Prepare weekly and monthly quality reports with KPIs and compile the final electrical quality dossier (as-built drawings, FAT/SAT reports, calibration records) for handover. Contract Management understands interactions between contract specifications, EPC quality obligations and project quality requirements Experience in management of multi split construction contracts is a plus HARD SKILLS: In-depth knowledge of the IEC 61400 series (including IEC 61400-24 lightning protection and IEC 61400-21 power quality), IEC 60502 and IEC 60840 (cables), IEC 60076 (transformers), IEC 62271 (switchgear) and IEC 61850 (substation communication). Knowledge of IEC 61936, IEEE 80 (earthing) and of the Egyptian grid code and EETC connection requirements. Ability to read and interpret single line diagrams, protection schemes, cable schedules and wiring diagrams. Hands-on knowledge of test equipment: insulation testers, VLF sets, relay test sets, earth testers and thermal cameras. ISO 9001 Lead Auditor certification and Thermography Level I/II are a plus. Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint…) and in document management and quality software tools (Aconex, SharePoint…). NEBOSH or IOSH certification is a plus. CPR and First Aid certification, or willingness to obtain Fluency in English is required. Arabic and French are real assets. SOFT SKILLS: Interpersonal: Integrity and independence, with the firmness to enforce quality requirements while keeping constructive relationships with contractors and suppliers Flexibility to interact and travel within multicultural and sometimes complex environments, with people coming from various levels of the Business environment (contractors, suppliers, grid operator, project managers, executives…) Collaborative and co-operative style: able to work as a team even in remote/virtual conditions Ability to work in high stress situations (commissioning and energisation milestones, grid operator constraints) Consultative in nature and in duties Technical: Field oriented, willing to work in desert and high temperature conditions Networking and communication skills: ability to coordinate testing teams, suppliers, WTG supplier and grid operator Ability to summarize and support the project decision-making process through a pragmatic and practical approach Ability to teach concepts and transfer quality knowledge to site teams Ability to translate technical jargon into simple concepts and clear reports Professional: Ability to adapt and prioritize tasks and workloads in accordance with project operational constraints Persuasive power and influence: manage stakeholder’s expectations by tailoring communications and reporting Thoroughness and organizational skills: good assessment capabilities, able to suggest improvements for activities involving itself and others Deadline-driven, results-oriented, and able to manage multiple work fronts and priorities simultaneously.
